items.q: line = 'Alice,30,"San Francisco, CA"'. What do len(line.split(',')) and len(next(csv.reader([line]))) give?
rationales: Not three pieces: split cuts at every comma, quoted or not, so it gives four, while the reader keeps the quoted field whole and gives three.
The reader respects the quotes, so it gives three fields, not four.
19 is the length of 'spam,eggs,bacon,ham' without the line terminator.
4 is the number of values, not the number of characters written.
The csv module does no conversion; a program calls int itself.
Only quoting=csv.QUOTE_NONNUMERIC reads unquoted values as floats.

items.q: A file saved by Excel as 'CSV UTF-8' starts with a byte order mark. It is read with open(name, encoding='utf-8'), and the first row is ['Name', 'City']. What is the first field of the row as Python sees it?
rationales: That is what encoding='utf-8-sig' gives, because it strips the mark.
utf-8 decodes the three bytes of the mark as the character U+FEFF without complaint; it stays in the first field.
JSON object keys are always strings, so the integer key comes back as the string '1'.
dumps accepts int keys and writes them as strings; it refuses only keys that are not str, int, float, bool or None.

items.q: A tuple (1, 2) is written with json.dumps and read back with json.loads. What comes back?
rationales: JSON has no tuple, so the round trip gives a list.
loads returns the Python value the text describes; the string is the text that dumps wrote.

options: It raises json.JSONDecodeError, a kind of ValueError
rationales: That is how a Python list literal behaves; JSON does not allow the trailing comma.
Nothing is added after the comma; the text is refused.
Every value in XML is text; a program converts it with int().
text is the string between the tags, here '1'; find returned the element and .text is its text.

items.q: In xmltodict, xmltodict.parse('1')['a']['b'] and xmltodict.parse('12')['a']['b'] have which types?
rationales: A repeated tag becomes a list and a single tag a plain value, so a program has to handle both shapes.
A single tag gives its text, not a list.

items.q: doc = ']>&e;&e;'. What does ET.fromstring(doc).text give, and what does defusedxml.ElementTree.fromstring(doc) do?
rationales: ElementTree expands an entity defined in the document itself, so the text is the expanded value.
defusedxml refuses documents that declare entities, which is why it is the choice for XML from an untrusted source.

items.q: A row a,,"" (the third field is an empty quoted string) is read with quoting=csv.QUOTE_NOTNULL. What does list(csv.reader(..., quoting=csv.QUOTE_NOTNULL)) give for that row?
rationales: With QUOTE_NOTNULL an empty field without quotes is read as None.
Only the unquoted empty field becomes None; the quoted one stays an empty string.
